newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows Dole with less than 50 percent in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Dole with less than 50 percent in Kansas.

text.p: A poll published Friday showed Bob Dole attracting less than 50 percent support in his home state of Kansas, but still leading President Clinton among Kansas voters by a comfortable margin.

The survey of 812 Kansans, conducted for the Kansas City Star by Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research, found that 49 percent supported Dole, 39 percent backed Clinton and six percent favored Reform Party candidate Ross Perot.
"The most dramatic news out of the Kansas poll, I think, is here's a favorite son who still can't poll above 50 percent," Del Ali, vice president of Mason-Dixon, said.
In neighboring Missouri, typically viewed as a bellwether for presidential races, the poll showed Clinton maintaining a lead over Dole.
Clinton claimed support of 46 percent of the 810 Missouri voters surveyed, with 37 percent for Dole and nine percent for Perot. Eight percent were undecided.
In each poll, the margin of error was plus or minus 3.5 percent.
